A working stack needs observation. Start by asking which service is failing, then inspect that service’s logs and dependencies.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Prepare your computer

Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers enabled and the .NET10 SDK. For the full SQL Server stack use supported x64 hardware with enough memory for SQL Server. WPF does not run in the Linux ASP.NET image. Accept applicable vendor licences yourself during installation. Run docker version and docker compose version in a terminal; start Docker Desktop if the engine cannot be reached.

Useful commands

docker compose ps
docker compose logs --tail 100 api
docker compose logs --tail 100 db
docker compose top
docker stats --no-stream
docker compose restart website
docker compose stop
docker compose start

ps shows state and published ports. logs shows startup/errors. stats shows resource use. restart does not rebuild changed source; use up --build for that. stop pauses the stack’s processes; down removes the stack containers/network but normally keeps named volumes.

Scaling without a port conflict

The supplied api publishes one fixed host port5100, so blindly using --scale api=2 will cause a host-port collision. For a scaling exercise, copy the Compose file, remove api’s host ports section, add expose:["8080"], keep internal service-name access and put a proper reverse proxy/load balancer in front. Then docker compose -f compose.scale.yaml up -d --scale api=2 can create replicas. Use a separate reviewed migration job before replicas start; do not let each production replica race a startup migration.

Troubleshooting table in words

  • db unhealthy: check password strength, memory, startup time, architecture support and SQL logs.
  • API migration error: verify generated migrations were copied into Api before image build, and check connection/permissions.
  • Website connection refused: wait for API readiness and check SchoolApi.
  • Port in use: change the host side or stop the conflicting process.
  • No matching image architecture: choose supported hardware or a compatible database alternative.
  • File changes not visible: rebuild the image and recreate the service; restarting an old image is not a rebuild.

Try it yourself

Why can service_started still lead to a temporary website failure?

Worked answer

It means the process was started, not that migrations and dependency checks are complete. Add/read readiness handling for a production design.

Should you solve every error by deleting volumes?

Worked answer

No. Diagnose first. Deleting volumes can erase the evidence and the data without fixing the underlying issue.
